Within each class the second negative has rates 1/4 and 3/4, so its likelihood ratio is 1/3; the odds become 1:9, which corresponds to probability 1/10.","transfer":"In this same model, calculate P(D | neither report flags) using the -- cell. What is P(D | both reports flag)?","options":["1/4","1/2","2/3","2/11"],"answer":3,"explanation":"The ++ cell contains 800 D files and 3,600 not-D files, giving 800/(800 + 3,600) = 2/11. Using the independent model's product would incorrectly produce 1/2.","transfer":"In this dependent model, what is P(D | first flags and second does not)? Which additional pair is sufficient for this update without assuming within-class independence?","options":["The two individual flag rates within D, without their overlap.","The both-flag rate within D and the both-flag rate within not-D.","The two individual flag rates within not-D, without their overlap.","The overall first-flag rate and the overall second-flag rate."],"answer":1,"explanation":"Let qD = P(F1+ and F2+ | D) and qN = P(F1+ and F2+ | not-D).
